νεκροὺς ἠλευθέρωσεν, ἐπεί πως τάφῳ διακονοῦσιν ἄγγελοι, πὼς δὲ λευχείμονες ὡς

τὸν Να ζαρηνὸν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον· οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν.
Τουτέστιν οὐρανὸς αὐτῷ τόπος, ἐκεῖ τὰ μύρα πέμψατε. Ἠγέρθη, οὐχ ἡμεῖς αὐτὸν
ἠγείραμεν. Ὑμῶν ἕνεκα τὸν λίθον ἐκυ λίσαμεν· πρὶν γὰρ ἡμᾶς καταβῆναι, ὁ τάφος
ἐκεκέ νωτο. Ἠγέρθη, καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτός.»
4 Ὃ ἄγγελος εἶπεν, οὐ χωρεῖ οὐδὲ προφήτης ἑρμηνεῦσαι· Ὡσηὲ τὸν καιρὸν
τῆς ἀναστάσεως λέγει, Ἠσαΐας οἶδεν, ἀλλὰ τὸ πῶς οὐκ ἐπίσταται. Ταῦτα μὲν γὰρ
Ὡσηὲ προφητείας τὰ ῥή ματα· «Πορευσώμεθα καὶ ἐπιστρέψωμεν πρὸς κύριον τὸν
θεὸν ἡμῶν, ὅτι αὐτὸς» πέπαικεν «καὶ ἰάσεται ἡμᾶς· πατάξει καὶ μο τώσει ἡμᾶς μετὰ
δύο ἡμέρας· ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ, ἀναστησό μεθα καὶ ζησόμεθα ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.»
Ἄκουε πάλιν ποῖα Ἠσαΐας ἐσάλπισεν· «Ἠισχύνθη ὁ Λίβανος, ἕλη ἐγένετο ὁ Σαρών.
orientation: Hesychius the homilist continues his proof that the one incarnate Word both died and as God freed the dead, now giving what the angels said to the women.
pass_a_gloss: For the one who as a dead man went down into Hades, this same one as God freed the dead, since in what way angels minister to a tomb, and in what way wearing white garments as for a bridegroom they appear to the women, and in what way to them they were saying: You seek Jesus of Nazareth the crucified; he is not here; for he was raised as he said. That is heaven is place for him, there send the ointments. He was raised, we did not raise him. For your sake we rolled the stone; for before we came down, the tomb had been emptied. He was raised, as he himself said. What the angel said, not even a prophet has room to interpret; Hosea tells the time of the Resurrection, Isaiah knows, but the how he does not know. For these are the words of the prophecy of Hosea: Let us go and let us return to the Lord our God, because he [verb uncertain] and he will heal us; he will strike and he will bandage us after two days; on the day the third, we will be raised and we will live before him. Hear again what things Isaiah trumpeted: Lebanon was shamed, Sharon became marshes.

pass_b_english: For the one who went down into Hades as one dead freed the dead as God. See how angels minister at the tomb, how they appear to the women wearing white garments as for a bridegroom, and how they spoke to them: "You seek Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He is not here, for he has risen, as he said (cf. Mark 16:6; Matthew 28:6). This means heaven is his place, so send the ointments there. He has risen; we did not raise him. We rolled the stone away for your sake, for the tomb already stood empty before we came down. He has risen, as he himself said."

What the angel said, not even a prophet can fully interpret. Hosea tells the time of the Resurrection, and Isaiah knows it, but he does not know how it happens. For these are Hosea's words of prophecy: "Let us go and return to the Lord our God, for he has struck us and he will heal us. He will strike us and bind us up after two days; on the third day we shall rise and live before him (Hosea 6:1-2)."
Listen again to what Isaiah trumpeted: "Lebanon is ashamed, Sharon has become a marsh (Isaiah 33:9)."
notes: Source has line break damage: Να ζαρηνὸν, ἐκυ λίσαμεν, ἐκεκέ νωτο, ῥή ματα; read as continuous words.
Hosea quotation reads πέπαικεν and μο τώσει where LXX Hosea 6:1 expects ἥρπακεν and μοτώσει / similar; gloss keeps what is printed and marks the verb uncertain.
Isaiah quotation breaks off mid verse in this section; gloss stops at ὁ Σαρών.

problems.why: The locked Greek text reads πέπαικεν ("has struck"), not LXX ἥρπακεν ("has torn"); English substitutes the standard Bible reading.
problems.ruling: Source πέπαικεν means 'has struck'; English 'torn' follows LXX ἥρπακεν, not this text.

problems.quote: He is not here, for he has risen, as he said (Mark 16:6).
problems.source_quote: οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν.
problems.why: Mark 16:6 supplies the preceding clause, but "He is not here, for he has risen, as he said" is verbatim Matthew 28:6 and not in Mark 16:6.
problems.fix: He is not here, for he has risen, as he said (cf. Mark 16:6; Matt 28:6).
problems.ruling: Greek οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν matches Matthew; Mark 16:6 citation is misleading.

problems.quote: He will strike us and bind us up. After two days, on the third day we shall rise
problems.source_quote:
πατάξει καὶ μο τώσει ἡμᾶς μετὰ
δύο ἡμέρας· ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ, ἀναστησό μεθα
problems.why: In Greek, "after two days" modifies "he will strike and bind us up" (ending with a semicolon), not "on the third day we shall rise."
problems.fix: He will strike us and bind us up after two days; on the third day we shall rise
problems.ruling: Source μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας ends strike/bind clause; English attaches it to third-day rising.

fixed: 'has torn us' misstates πέπαικεν ('has struck'), not LXX ἥρπακεν: changed to 'has struck us'.
'as he said (Mark 16:6)' misattributes οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν, verbatim Matthew 28:6: expanded citation to Mark 16:6 and Matthew 28:6.
'After two days' misplaced: source has μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας· with the preceding πατάξει καὶ μοτώσει clause, not with ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ: moved to preceding clause.
